## What this notebook shows {.unnumbered}

This notebook goes through every component of the
[GSM2_Julia](https://github.com/francescogcordoni/GSM2_Julia) framework on a
single, small spheroid, so that it runs in a few minutes on a laptop. It
complements the two scripts it is built on:

- [`example/spheroid.jl`](https://github.com/francescogcordoni/GSM2_Julia/blob/main/example/spheroid.jl):
  monoenergetic beam, full pipeline;
- [`example/spheroid_poly.jl`](https://github.com/francescogcordoni/GSM2_Julia/blob/main/example/spheroid_poly.jl):
  beam made of a few discrete energies.

Here the beam is **polyenergetic**, with a **Gaussian energy spectrum**, and the
**track-segment condition is switched off** (`track_seg = false`): every particle
loses energy along its path, so cells at different depths see different energies
and LET. The sections are:

| Section | Feature |
|---|---|
| [Beam](#a-gaussian-polyenergetic-beam) | Gaussian energy spectrum, discretised into bins; fluence weights; dose-averaged LET |
| [Energy loss](#energy-loss-along-the-path) | `track_seg = false`: energy and LET layer by layer (CSDA range) |
| [Dose and damage](#dose-and-dna-damage) | Monte Carlo dose and lesions, per energy bin and summed |
| [Survival and fate](#survival-and-fate) | Exact GSM² survival, incremental fate model, clonogenic survival |
| [ABM](#agent-based-dynamics-and-a-second-fraction) | Delayed death, lineage tracking, a second fraction with re-oxygenation |
| [Options](#biological-options) | Contact-inhibition threshold, growth plateau, migration, G2 checkpoint |
| [Continuous irradiation](#continuous-low-dose-rate-irradiation) | Low-dose-rate exposure with concurrent cell dynamics |
| [Engine check](#event-engine-validation) | Heap engine vs original loop |

Render with `quarto render example/features_walkthrough.qmd` (Julia ≥ 1.10 with
the packages listed in the README, and the Quarto Julia engine).

## Setup

The utilities are included in `Main`, because the setup functions write their
results (the cell table, the irradiation conditions, …) as globals of `Main`.
The notebook then copies those globals into its own scope with `pull!`.

```{julia}
#| label: setup
#| output: false

import Pkg
Pkg.activate(joinpath(homedir(), ".julia", "environments",
                      "v$(VERSION.major).$(VERSION.minor)"))

using Base.Threads, CSV, DataFrames, Distributions, Random, Printf
using Plots, StatsPlots, Statistics, StatsBase
ENV["GKSwstype"] = "100"          # headless GR

@eval Main begin
    using Base.Threads, Distributed, CSV, DataFrames, Distributions, Random
    using Plots, StatsPlots, Statistics, StatsBase, ProgressBars, ProgressMeter
    using GLM, Optim, LsqFit, JLD2, DelimitedFiles
    using InlineStrings, SparseArrays, Printf, CUDA
    using Statistics: mean
end
Base.include(Main, joinpath(@__DIR__, "..", "src", "load_utilities.jl"))

using Main: GSM2, Ion, Irrad, AT, CellPopulation, SimulationTimeSeries
import Main: setup_GSM2!, setup_IonIrrad!, setup_cell_lattice!, setup_cell_population!,
             setup_irrad_conditions!, set_oxygen_diffusion!, calculate_beam_properties,
             load_stopping_power, table_for, let_at, validate_stopping,
             calculate_OER, calculate_kappa,
             MC_dose_damage_poly!, domain_GSM2, survival_ci,
             set_fate_model!, set_checkpoint!, set_quiescence_threshold!,
             set_division_limit!, clear_division_limit!,
             set_founder_tracking!, clear_founder_tracking!, founders,
             compute_times_domain!, run_simulation_abm!, run_simulation_abm_migration!,
             irradiate_continuous_abm!, compare_engines, _advance_idle!,
             print_phase_distribution, plot_cell_cycle_distribution,
             plot_scalar_cell, plot_scalar_cell_poly, plot_damage_poly, plot_times,
             plot_phase_dynamics, plot_spatial_distribution

sp = load_stopping_power()
@eval Main sp = $sp

"Copy globals written into Main by the setup functions into this notebook."
function pull!(syms...)
    for s in syms
        isdefined(Main, s) && Core.eval(@__MODULE__, :($s = Main.$s))
    end
end

"Radius of the current spheroid (µm), from the alive cells."
function current_radius(df)
    a = df.is_cell .== 1
    cx, cy, cz = mean(df.x[a]), mean(df.y[a]), mean(df.z[a])
    maximum(sqrt.((df.x[a] .- cx).^2 .+ (df.y[a] .- cy).^2 .+ (df.z[a] .- cz).^2)) + 15.0
end

gr(); default(framestyle = :box, grid = true, gridalpha = 0.3, lw = 2)
println("Threads: ", nthreads())
```

## Parameters

All choices are in one place. The spheroid is small (radius 200 µm, about 1200
cells) so that every section runs quickly; the energy is chosen low enough for
the energy loss across the spheroid to be visible.

```{julia}
#| label: parameters
#| output: false

# Beam: Gaussian energy spectrum
PARTICLE   = "12C"
E_MEAN     = 20.0      # mean kinetic energy (MeV/u)
E_SIGMA    = 1.0       # standard deviation (MeV/u)
N_BINS     = 7         # energy bins used to discretise the spectrum
N_SIGMA    = 2.5       # spectrum truncated at ±N_SIGMA·σ
DOSE_GY    = 2.0       # dose per fraction, at the entrance of the target (Gy)

# Geometry
TUMOR_RADIUS = 200.0;  R_CELL = 15.0;  X_BOX = 400.0;  X_VOXEL = 800.0
RD = 0.8;  RN = 7.2

# Physics and run options
TYPE_AT     = "KC"     # Kiefer–Chatterjee amorphous track
TRACK_SEG   = false    # energy loss along the path
TARGET_GEOM = "circle"; CALC_TYPE = "full"
NAT_APO     = 1e-10
T_BETWEEN   = 24.0     # h between the two fractions
T_AFTER     = 72.0     # h of follow-up after the second fraction

# GSM² rates (h⁻¹), calibrated on phase-specific LQ data
gsm2_cycle = [GSM2(2.7805, 0.01287, 0.04030, RD, RN),   # G1 / G0
              GSM2(5.8401, 0.00589, 0.05794, RD, RN),   # S
              GSM2(1.7720, 0.02431, 5.705e-5, RD, RN),  # G2 / M
              GSM2(2.5657, 0.01481, 0.01266, RD, RN)]   # average

validate_stopping(sp, PARTICLE, parse(Int, match(r"\d+", PARTICLE).match))
Random.seed!(2026)
```

---

## A Gaussian polyenergetic beam

A real beam has an energy spread. Here the kinetic energy follows a Gaussian
distribution, $E \sim \mathcal{N}(\bar E, \sigma^2)$, truncated at
$\pm 2.5\sigma$ and discretised into `N_BINS` bins. Each bin $i$ is a
monoenergetic component with energy $E_i$ (the bin centre) and **fluence
fraction** $w_i$ (the Gaussian probability of the bin).

The prescribed dose fixes the total fluence. Since each particle of bin $i$
deposits a dose proportional to its LET,
$D = 1.602\times10^{-9} \, F_{\mathrm{tot}} \sum_i w_i \, \mathrm{LET}_i$, so

$$
F_{\mathrm{tot}} = \frac{D}{1.602\times10^{-9}\sum_i w_i\,\mathrm{LET}_i},
\qquad N_i = w_i\,F_{\mathrm{tot}}\,\pi R_{\mathrm{beam}}^2 .
$$

```{julia}
#| label: spectrum

edges    = range(E_MEAN - N_SIGMA * E_SIGMA, E_MEAN + N_SIGMA * E_SIGMA; length = N_BINS + 1)
ENERGIES = collect(0.5 .* (edges[1:end-1] .+ edges[2:end]))
W        = diff(cdf.(Normal(E_MEAN, E_SIGMA), collect(edges)));  W ./= sum(W)
PARTICLES = fill(PARTICLE, N_BINS)

tab   = table_for(sp, PARTICLE)
LET_i = [let_at(tab, E) for E in ENERGIES]
LET_F = sum(W .* LET_i)                         # fluence-averaged LET
LET_D = sum(W .* LET_i .^ 2) / sum(W .* LET_i)  # dose-averaged LET
@printf("Fluence-averaged LET %.1f keV/µm, dose-averaged LET %.1f keV/µm\n", LET_F, LET_D)

p1 = bar(ENERGIES, W; bar_width = step(edges), xlabel = "Kinetic energy (MeV/u)",
         ylabel = "Fluence fraction", label = "bins", color = :steelblue, alpha = 0.7)
Eg = range(first(edges), last(edges); length = 200)
plot!(p1, Eg, pdf.(Normal(E_MEAN, E_SIGMA), Eg) .* step(edges); color = :black, label = "Gaussian")
p2 = scatter(ENERGIES, LET_i; xlabel = "Kinetic energy (MeV/u)", ylabel = "LET (keV/µm)",
             label = "", color = :firebrick)
plot(p1, p2; layout = (1, 2), size = (900, 340))
```

## Spheroid and irradiation conditions

The spheroid is built on a cubic lattice and oxygenated with the
reaction–diffusion profile, which is computed from the local cell density
(`density = :radial`).

```{julia}
#| label: build

setup_GSM2!(2.5657, 0.01481, 0.01266, RD, RN)
setup_IonIrrad!(DOSE_GY, ENERGIES, PARTICLES; type_AT = TYPE_AT)   # one Ion per bin

N_sideVox   = Int(floor(2 * X_BOX / X_VOXEL))
N_CellsSide = 2 * convert(Int64, floor(X_BOX / (2 * R_CELL)))
setup_cell_lattice!(TARGET_GEOM, X_BOX, R_CELL, N_sideVox, N_CellsSide;
                    ParIrr = "false", track_seg = TRACK_SEG, full_cycle = true)
@eval Main begin
    tumor_radius = $TUMOR_RADIUS; X_voxel = $X_VOXEL; X_box = $X_BOX
end
setup_cell_population!(TARGET_GEOM, X_BOX, R_CELL, N_sideVox, N_CellsSide,
                       gsm2_cycle[4]; ParIrr = "false")
pull!(:gsm2, :ion, :irrad, :LET, :cell_df, :df_center_x, :df_center_y, :at)

setup_irrad_conditions!(ion, irrad, TYPE_AT, cell_df, TRACK_SEG)    # one set per bin
pull!(:irrad_cond, :irrad_cond_original_layers, :lets, :energies, :cell_df)

set_oxygen_diffusion!(cell_df; density = :radial)

N_init = count(==(1), cell_df.is_cell)
println("Spheroid: $N_init cells")
print_phase_distribution(cell_df; label = "pre-irradiation")
cell_df_pristine = deepcopy(cell_df)
```

```{julia}
#| label: fig-oxygen
#| fig-cap: "Oxygen level of each cell as a function of its distance from the centre."

a  = cell_df.is_cell .== 1
cx = mean(cell_df.x[a]); cy = mean(cell_df.y[a]); cz = mean(cell_df.z[a])
r  = sqrt.((cell_df.x[a] .- cx).^2 .+ (cell_df.y[a] .- cy).^2 .+ (cell_df.z[a] .- cz).^2)
scatter(r, cell_df.O[a]; ms = 2, msw = 0, alpha = 0.5, label = "",
        xlabel = "Distance from the centre (µm)", ylabel = "O₂ (%)")
```

## Energy loss along the path

With `track_seg = false`, the target is divided into layers perpendicular to the
beam, one per lattice plane. For each energy bin, the energy at the next layer is
obtained by range inversion, $E_{i+1} = R^{-1}\!\left(R(E_i) - h\right)$, where
$R(E)$ is the continuous-slowing-down range computed from the stopping-power
table; the LET and the track parameters are then recomputed at $E_{i+1}$. Empty
layers do not absorb, so the depth is measured from the surface of the spheroid.

```{julia}
#| label: fig-let-depth
#| fig-cap: "Kinetic energy and LET of each energy bin as a function of depth. Dashed: LET at the entrance, i.e. the value used under the track-segment condition."

zs   = sort(unique(cell_df.z))
cols = palette(:viridis, N_BINS)
pE = plot(xlabel = "z (µm)", ylabel = "Energy (MeV/u)", legend = false)
pL = plot(xlabel = "z (µm)", ylabel = "LET (keV/µm)", legend = :topleft)
for i in 1:N_BINS
    plot!(pE, zs, energies[i]; color = cols[i])
    plot!(pL, zs, lets[i]; color = cols[i], label = @sprintf("%.1f MeV/u", ENERGIES[i]))
    hline!(pL, [lets[i][1]]; color = cols[i], ls = :dash, lw = 1, label = "")
end
plot(pE, pL; layout = (1, 2), size = (950, 360))
```

## Dose and DNA damage

The number of particles of each bin follows from the fluence weights. Dose and
lesions are computed bin by bin and summed per cell (`MC_dose_damage_poly!`).

```{julia}
#| label: dose

R_beam, _, _ = calculate_beam_properties(CALC_TYPE, TARGET_GEOM, X_BOX, X_VOXEL,
                                         current_radius(cell_df))
F_tot     = DOSE_GY / (1.602e-9 * sum(W .* LET))     # particles / cm²
Npar_vect = round.(Int, W .* F_tot .* π .* R_beam^2 .* 1e-8)
println("Particles per bin: ", Npar_vect)

@time MC_dose_damage_poly!(ion, Npar_vect, R_beam, irrad_cond, cell_df,
                           df_center_x, df_center_y, at, gsm2_cycle, TYPE_AT, TRACK_SEG)
a = cell_df.is_cell .== 1
@printf("Mean cell dose %.2f Gy (prescribed at the entrance: %.2f Gy)\n",
        mean(cell_df.dose_cell[a]), DOSE_GY)
```

```{julia}
#| label: fig-dose
#| fig-cap: "Cell dose: distribution and 3-D map (left), and grouped by depth layer (right)."

display(plot_scalar_cell_poly(cell_df, :dose_cell))
display(plot_scalar_cell_poly(cell_df, :dose_cell; layer_plot = true))
```

```{julia}
#| label: fig-depth-dose
#| fig-cap: "Mean cell dose as a function of depth: the dose rises with depth as the particles slow down."

g = combine(groupby(cell_df[a, :], :z), :dose_cell => mean => :d)
sort!(g, :z)
plot(g.z, g.d; marker = :circle, ms = 3, xlabel = "z (µm)", ylabel = "Mean cell dose (Gy)",
     label = "", color = :firebrick)
```

```{julia}
#| label: fig-damage
#| fig-cap: "Sublethal (X) lesions per cell, all bins and per bin."

display(plot_damage_poly(cell_df))
display(plot_damage_poly(cell_df; pp = true, particles = PARTICLES))
```

## Survival and fate

The survival probability of each cell is the exact GSM² probability of
completing repair. Fates are then sampled with the **incremental** model: a
lethally damaged cell becomes *doomed*, keeps its site and is removed after a
phase-dependent delay. The **clonogenic** surviving fraction (alive and not
doomed) must agree with the mean survival probability.

```{julia}
#| label: survival

set_fate_model!(:incremental)
set_checkpoint!(:all)

# Survival without resetting the cells' clocks (needed by the incremental model)
for i in findall(==(1), cell_df.is_cell)
    ph = cell_df.cell_cycle[i]
    gs = (ph == "G1" || ph == "G0") ? gsm2_cycle[1] : ph == "S" ? gsm2_cycle[2] : gsm2_cycle[3]
    cell_df.sp[i] = domain_GSM2(cell_df.dam_X_dom[i], cell_df.dam_Y_dom[i], gs)
end
SF_gsm2 = mean(cell_df.sp[cell_df.is_cell .== 1])

compute_times_domain!(cell_df, gsm2_cycle; nat_apo = NAT_APO, terminal_time = Inf, summary = true)
SF_clono = count((cell_df.is_cell .== 1) .& .!isfinite.(cell_df.death_time)) / N_init
@printf("Mean GSM² survival %.3f   clonogenic survival %.3f\n", SF_gsm2, SF_clono)
```

```{julia}
#| label: fig-survival
#| fig-cap: "Survival probability of each cell (log scale) and its 3-D map."

display(plot_scalar_cell(cell_df, :sp; xscale = :log10))
```

```{julia}
#| label: fig-times
#| fig-cap: "Times of repair completion and of radiation-induced death."

display(plot_times(cell_df; show_means = true))
```

## Agent-based dynamics and a second fraction

Lineage tracking is switched on before the ABM, so that every surviving clone
can be followed. After `T_BETWEEN` hours a second fraction is delivered to the
**current** spheroid: the oxygen profile is recomputed, the beam covers the
current radius, the energy loss is recomputed on the current cell configuration,
and fates are assigned only to cells that are not already doomed.

```{julia}
#| label: fraction-1-abm

set_founder_tracking!(cell_df)
ts1, _ = run_simulation_abm!(cell_df; nat_apo = NAT_APO, terminal_time = T_BETWEEN,
                             snapshot_times = Int[], verbose = false,
                             return_dataframes = false, update_input = true)
_advance_idle!(cell_df, T_BETWEEN - (isempty(ts1.time) ? 0.0 : ts1.time[end]))
n_doomed = count((cell_df.is_cell .== 1) .& isfinite.(cell_df.death_time))
println("At the second fraction: $(count(==(1), cell_df.is_cell)) cells, $n_doomed doomed")
```

```{julia}
#| label: fraction-2

set_oxygen_diffusion!(cell_df; density = :radial)                 # re-oxygenation
setup_IonIrrad!(DOSE_GY, ENERGIES, PARTICLES; type_AT = TYPE_AT)
pull!(:ion, :irrad, :LET)
setup_irrad_conditions!(ion, irrad, TYPE_AT, cell_df, TRACK_SEG)  # on the current spheroid
pull!(:irrad_cond, :lets, :energies, :cell_df)

R_now = current_radius(cell_df)
R_beam, _, _ = calculate_beam_properties(CALC_TYPE, TARGET_GEOM, X_BOX, X_VOXEL, R_now)
Npar_vect = round.(Int, W .* (DOSE_GY / (1.602e-9 * sum(W .* LET))) .* π .* R_beam^2 .* 1e-8)
MC_dose_damage_poly!(ion, Npar_vect, R_beam, irrad_cond, cell_df,
                     df_center_x, df_center_y, at, gsm2_cycle, TYPE_AT, TRACK_SEG)

before = count((cell_df.is_cell .== 1) .& .!isfinite.(cell_df.death_time))
compute_times_domain!(cell_df, gsm2_cycle; nat_apo = NAT_APO, terminal_time = Inf)
after  = count((cell_df.is_cell .== 1) .& .!isfinite.(cell_df.death_time))
@printf("Spheroid radius %.0f µm; surviving fraction of the second fraction %.3f\n",
        R_now, after / before)

ts2, snaps = run_simulation_abm!(cell_df; nat_apo = NAT_APO, terminal_time = T_AFTER,
                                 snapshot_times = [0, 24, 48, 72], verbose = false,
                                 return_dataframes = true, update_input = true)
```

```{julia}
#| label: fig-dynamics
#| fig-cap: "Total cells over both fractions (dashed: the two fractions) and cell-cycle phases after the second fraction."

t_all = vcat(ts1.time, ts2.time .+ T_BETWEEN)
n_all = vcat(ts1.total_cells, ts2.total_cells)
pT = plot(t_all, n_all; xlabel = "Time after the first fraction (h)", ylabel = "Total cells",
          label = "", color = :black)
vline!(pT, [0.0, T_BETWEEN]; ls = :dash, color = :gray, label = "")
plot(pT, plot_phase_dynamics(ts2); layout = (1, 2), size = (1000, 360))
```

```{julia}
#| label: fig-snapshot
#| fig-cap: "The spheroid 72 h after the second fraction, coloured by cell-cycle phase."

display(plot_spatial_distribution(snaps[maximum(keys(snaps))]; color_by = :cell_cycle))
```

```{julia}
#| label: fig-clones
#| fig-cap: "Size of the surviving clones at the end of the follow-up (lineage tracking)."

F     = founders()
alive = (cell_df.is_cell .== 1) .& .!isfinite.(cell_df.death_time)
sizes = collect(values(countmap(F[alive .& (F .> 0)])))
clear_founder_tracking!()
@printf("%d surviving clones; largest %d cells\n", length(sizes), maximum(sizes))
histogram(sizes; bins = 30, xlabel = "Clone size (cells)", ylabel = "Number of clones",
          label = "", color = :seagreen, yscale = :log10)
```

## Biological options

Each option is global: it is set before a run and reset afterwards. All runs in
this section start from copies of the unirradiated spheroid and last 72 h.

```{julia}
#| label: options

control(df; kw...) = run_simulation_abm!(df; nat_apo = NAT_APO, terminal_time = 72.0,
                                         snapshot_times = Int[], verbose = false,
                                         return_dataframes = false, update_input = true, kw...)

# Reference
d0 = deepcopy(cell_df_pristine);  ts_ref, _ = control(d0)

# Contact inhibition: quiescent when at most 2 of the 26 neighbours are empty
dq = deepcopy(cell_df_pristine)
set_quiescence_threshold!(2; cell_df = dq);  ts_q, _ = control(dq)
set_quiescence_threshold!(0; cell_df = dq)

# Growth plateau: division probability falls off beyond R50
dl = deepcopy(cell_df_pristine)
set_division_limit!(dl; R50 = TUMOR_RADIUS + 60.0, w = 15.0);  ts_l, _ = control(dl)
clear_division_limit!()

# Migration: random walk with motility D_m (µm²/h) on a lattice of spacing 2R_cell
dm = deepcopy(cell_df_pristine)
ts_m, _ = run_simulation_abm_migration!(dm, 50.0, 2R_CELL; nat_apo = NAT_APO,
                                        terminal_time = 72.0, snapshot_times = Int[],
                                        verbose = false, return_dataframes = false)

plot(ts_ref.time, ts_ref.total_cells; label = "reference", color = :black,
     xlabel = "Time (h)", ylabel = "Total cells (unirradiated)")
plot!(ts_q.time, ts_q.total_cells; label = "quiescence threshold k = 2", color = :steelblue)
plot!(ts_l.time, ts_l.total_cells; label = "growth plateau", color = :darkorange)
plot!(ts_m.time, ts_m.total_cells; label = "migration, D = 50 µm²/h", color = :seagreen)
```

The cell-cycle checkpoint can also be changed: with `set_checkpoint!(:g2)`,
damaged cells keep cycling through G1 and S and are held only in G2, instead of
being arrested in every phase (`:all`, the default). The continuous irradiation
below uses it.

---

## Continuous low-dose-rate irradiation

`irradiate_continuous_abm!` delivers the dose as a train of short pulses, with
repair, fate assignment and cell dynamics running between pulses, so that
redistribution and repopulation take place during the exposure. It uses uniform
(low-LET) damage; here, 2 Gy of 100 MeV protons at 0.5 Gy/h.

```{julia}
#| label: continuous

LET_p = let_at(table_for(sp, "1H"), 100.0)
K_tot = 9.0 * calculate_kappa("1H", LET_p, 21.0)     # X lesions per cell per Gy
dc    = deepcopy(cell_df_pristine)
ts_c, res = irradiate_continuous_abm!(dc, gsm2_cycle; dose = 2.0, dose_rate_gyh = 0.5,
                                      K_tot = K_tot, L_tot = 1e-3 * K_tot,
                                      checkpoint = :g2, seed = 1)
set_checkpoint!(:all)
@printf("Clonogenic fraction at the end of exposure %.3f; clonogenic cells / initial %.3f\n",
        res.SF_plated, res.N_rel)
display(plot_phase_dynamics(ts_c))
```

---

## Event engine validation

The default engine stores the next event of every cell in a binary min-heap and
updates only the neighbours of each event. `compare_engines` runs it and the
original loop from the same state and seed and checks that the trajectories
coincide.

```{julia}
#| label: engines

compare_engines(cell_df_pristine; seed = 1, terminal_time = 24.0)
```

---

## Where to go next {.unnumbered}

- Change `PARTICLE`, `E_MEAN`, `E_SIGMA` and `N_BINS` to explore other spectra;
  `N_BINS = 1` with `E_SIGMA` small recovers a monoenergetic beam.
- Set `TRACK_SEG = true` to compare with the track-segment condition (all layers
  at the entrance energy).
- The scripts in `scripts/` reproduce the figures of the paper; see the README.
